hardware: this Mac (release build, whisper.cpp Metal, 4 threads)

sets.ami_headset_tracks: 5 single-speaker 10-minute AMI headset tracks (benchmarks/prepare_ami.py); spontaneous speech. Absolute WER is high (about 20%) and only partly explained by scoring conventions: contractions such as wanna/gonna and dropped backchannels such as 'yeah' account for a small share, the rest was not categorized.

findings: The speech-aligned pipeline beats the old fixed 60 s windows on sparse meeting-like tracks with the same small.en model: AMI WER 24.3% -> 20.8% (deletions 282 -> 230, insertions 115 -> 56).
large-v3 is most accurate on read speech (2.0% vs small.en 3.1%) and ties medium.en on AMI (19.5%); the AMI gap between models is within about 1 point, so it does not separate them.
large-v3-turbo was not more accurate than small.en on AMI.
All models run far faster than real time (large-v3 about 0.12-0.18 RTF), so a one-hour meeting transcribes in roughly 7-11 minutes.
